surface: Goals creation, route planning, returning room, recovery, and plan progression
scope: Put a local explainable planning and recovery engine behind the existing threshold-room spectacle. Derive the first Quest from the person's aim and reality, persist an editable route, advance only from exact current-marker evidence, adapt honestly when the plan does not fit, preserve old proof, and expose that logic through the authored room rather than a dashboard.
user_job: Tell Room of Days what I am actually trying to change, receive a credible route and first move, and return after imperfect days without having to re-plan or feel that the app has lost the point.

active_sources.judged_state: The owner rejected a spectacle-only implementation and required aim-derived first action, an actual plan, psychology-backed recovery, preserved proof, and stronger exact-action button copy.
active_sources.viewport: Product contract applies to the authored 430x932 modern-iPhone journey and persisted behavior across returns

superseded_sources.reason: The owner said the room looked better but did not back its spectacle with coherent logistics, aim-derived action, a real plan, or the promised psychology.

product.decision: A goal is an owned, persisted route from stated outcome and current reality to visible proof, not a title plus a sorted Quest pile. Route type, available time, snag, progress, revision, attempt, and prior proof all affect what the app serves next.
product.proof: A production-equivalent goal produces a four-marker editable route and exact first Quest from its entered aim, reality, proof, time, and snag; only current marker identity can progress it; hard-day recovery returns to the intended repeated action; routine and legacy paths remain coherent.

interaction.decision: Creation moves through AIM, REALITY, and ROUTE; the person can edit markers before accepting. Returning shows one reasoned action and a visible plan-does-not-fit path whose chosen signal immediately changes the current marker without erasing earned proof.
interaction.proof: Stable interaction tests traverse creation, editing, opening, exact Quest handoff, stale and out-of-order rejection, recalibration, recovery restoration, changed outcome, legacy upgrade, routine continuation, and Reduced Motion.

visual.decision: The room remains the interface, but its inscriptions now expose real plan state: marker position and reason belong above the exact action, the brass threshold uses a short specific verb-object label, and plan adjustment is a visible secondary physical route.
visual.proof: Fresh 430x932 renders show AIM, REALITY, ROUTE, active threshold, adjusted threshold, opening arrival, and goal folio with readable exact-action typography, route progress, proof, and adjustment history.

anti_fallbacks.fallback: Choosing the next Quest by due date, difficulty, or words found in the goal title
anti_fallbacks.why: That recreates the rejected illusion of intelligence and can serve an unrelated or semantically wrong first action.

anti_fallbacks.fallback: Treating a generated four-item list as a plan without marker identity, revisions, attempts, proof, or recovery state
anti_fallbacks.why: The route would be decorative copy because stale, duplicated, or out-of-order tasks could still fake progress.

anti_fallbacks.fallback: Using motivational spectacle, vague Step in copy, or guilt language where the software lacks a defensible next move
anti_fallbacks.why: The room must earn excitement through useful logistics and honest adaptation rather than hype alone.

first_real_slice.scenario: Create a calm-apartment reset goal from a crowded counter reality, accept the drafted route, return to marker one, say it is too big, complete the smaller proof, and continue on the intended route.
first_real_slice.real_inputs: Outcome: use the kitchen without feeling overwhelmed; reality: the counter is crowded; proof: it stays usable for a normal week; capacity: 15 minutes; snag: the whole thing feels too big after class.
first_real_slice.user_action: Complete AIM and REALITY, edit or accept ROUTE, start the exact first Quest, then choose plan does not fit and take the hand-sized rescue.
first_real_slice.expected_outcome: The app drafts a counter-specific route, serves only marker one, records exact proof, keeps the same goal selected during adjustment, counts the rescue honestly, and restores the intended repeated action for the next attempt.
first_real_slice.state_boundary: GoalPlan and Quest route identity persist through JSON; plan revision invalidates stale Quests; GameState commit alone advances current evidence; prior progress and first proof survive route construction and recalibration.

required_states.state: AIM, REALITY, and editable ROUTE before acceptance
required_states.why_can_disprove: The engine can still be a template if the first action ignores the entered reality, proof, capacity, or selected route type.

required_states.state: Returning threshold with current marker, reason, exact action, CTA, fallback, and adjustment route
required_states.why_can_disprove: The plan can be real in storage but remain incomprehensible or visually detached in the room.

required_states.state: Too-big adjustment, smaller proof, retained history, and restored repeated marker
required_states.why_can_disprove: Recovery can erase progress, permanently dilute the plan, or advance from a stale Quest even when the happy path works.

ripple_map.state: Earlier progress and first proof already exist
ripple_map.expected_effect: Build a real route in place while preserving the numerical progress and proof earned before route support existed.
ripple_map.verification_plan: Run the legacy route-upgrade widget journey and engine test that starts at seven of ten before adding a route.

ripple_map.state: Final review marker completes after real repetitions
ripple_map.expected_effect: Keep the earned anchor, increment the evidence cycle, issue fresh route identity, and return to a workable repeated action rather than ending the goal.
ripple_map.verification_plan: Complete an entire routine through GameState and assert the next cycle, revision, anchor, and open current marker.

ripple_map.surface_or_primitive: Route engine domain and fallback action selection
ripple_map.state: Study, skill, creative, care, people, admin, movement, and unfamiliar goals
ripple_map.expected_effect: Use explicit outcome and reality ahead of the default stat, produce distinct route structures, and fall back to a bounded generic starting proof without pretending to know more than was entered.
ripple_map.verification_plan: Exercise route-type and explicit-aim tests, then owner-test at least one goal unlike the apartment fixture.

unverified_property: Whether the drafted route feels meaningfully insightful for the owner's own unusual goal on a physical phone, rather than merely coherent for deterministic fixtures and known domain vocabulary.

decisive_check.method: Create one real owner goal on the phone, read the full drafted route, use plan does not fit once, and return after completing the smaller proof.
decisive_check.target: The owner's normal iPhone-class device and a goal unlike the calm-apartment fixture
decisive_check.pass_condition: The owner says the first move feels earned by what they entered, understands the route without explanation, and sees the app preserve direction and proof after a hard-day adjustment.
